name: Port Moresby Nature Park
note: Wildlife and botanical park (formerly the National Capital Botanical Gardens) with tree kangaroos, cassowaries, birds of paradise, a WWII walk-through aviary and gardens.

name: National Museum and Art Gallery
wiki: Papua New Guinea National Museum and Art Gallery
note: Museum: PNG's national museum in Waigani, with carvings, beads, traditional boats, cultural objects and WWII relics outside.

name: Ela Beach
note: Beach: the revitalised waterfront in central Port Moresby, a paved promenade for walks and sunsets, with weekend markets and cultural events (not a swimming beach).
coordinates_source: WV Port Moresby listing geo (Ela Beach Craft Market point on the beach; no OSM "Ela Beach" feature found, check)

name: Bomana War Cemetery
note: War cemetery: the largest WWII Commonwealth cemetery in PNG, 3,824 graves, mostly from the Kokoda campaign; free and open daily, 19 km out of town.

name: National Parliament of Papua New Guinea
wiki: National Parliament of Papua New Guinea
note: Landmark: the parliament building in Waigani, designed on a Maprik haus tambaran; visitors see the exterior, with guided tours outside sitting days.

name: Gordons Market
note: Market: a daily city market in Gordons with produce, betel nut, crafts and bilums; best visited in the morning with a guide.
coordinates_source: photon OSM amenity=marketplace "Gordons Market" (resolver LOW, hand-graded; verify)

name: Loloata Island
note: Island: a private island resort in Bootless Inlet, 20-30 minutes by boat from Port Moresby, with snorkelling, diving, kayaks and day visits.
coordinates_source: photon OSM leisure=resort "Loloata Island Resort" (the visitor point on the island; resolver LOW, verify)

name: Adventure Park PNG
note: Family amusement park at 14 Mile, outside the city, with a Ferris wheel, water slides, paddle boats, a small zoo, lakes and gardens.

name: Varirata National Park
note: National park: PNG's first national park, 23 km NE of Port Moresby on the Sogeri Plateau, with lookouts, a lake, trails, birdwatching and picnic areas; admission charged.

name: Sogeri Plateau
note: Natural area: 600 m plateau 'a popular weekend trip' from Port Moresby, with picnic sites, rapids and walks (Wikipedia article is the town of Sogeri on the plateau).

name: Kerema
note: Town: the capital of Gulf Province on the Gulf of Papua coast, a basic base for the Gulf with a few hotels, reached by the Hiritano Highway or by air.

name: Kikori
note: Town: a small fishing centre on the Kikori River delta, a good birdwatching base with Delta Lodge.

name: Goroka
note: Town: provincial capital of Eastern Highlands and the base for the Goroka Show, Asaro Mudmen and Mount Michael; the region's main hub (base).

name: Mount Hagen
note: Town: provincial capital of Western Highlands and the regional air hub (Kagamuga Airport); base for Kuk, Hagen Show, Baiyer River and Mount Hagen Market.

name: Kainantu
note: Town: market town on the Highlands Highway with the Eastern Highlands Cultural Centre and pottery; a stop between Lae and Goroka.

name: Mendi
note: Town: provincial capital of Southern Highlands; gateway to Lake Kutubu and Mount Giluwe, with a Friday and Saturday market.

name: Kundiawa
note: Town: capital of Simbu (Chimbu) Province; the departure point for the Mount Wilhelm climb, reached from Keglsugl.

name: Tari
note: Town: capital of Hela Province and base for the Huli wigmen, Tari Basin and Ambua Lodge. No Wikivoyage article exists (404).

name: Mount Wilhelm
note: Mountain: Papua New Guinea's highest peak (4,509 m), climbed by guided treks from Keglsugl (Simbu) or Ambullua (Western Highlands).
coordinates_source: osm natural=peak node (MEDIUM; Wikipedia coordinates are rounded)

name: Mount Giluwe
note: Mountain: second-highest peak in PNG (4,368 m), a shield volcano with guided climbs, in Southern Highlands.

name: Mount Michael
note: Mountain: cloud-forest hill near Goroka with hiking trails and highland views. The Wikipedia title Mount Michael is the South Sandwich Islands volcano, so it is not used.

name: Lake Kutubu
note: Lake: 800 m upland lake, about 50 km southwest of Mendi, with Ramsar status and endemic fish; reached by road and boat.

name: Asaro Mudmen
note: Cultural attraction: masked mud-men performers from the Asaro people, who live in a village near Goroka; the tourism board names the village performances.

name: Eastern Highlands Cultural Centre and Museum
note: Museum: cultural centre and museum at Kainantu, known for its pottery and the Kainantu pottery and weaving markets. No dedicated Wikipedia article found.

name: J.K. McCarthy Museum
note: Museum: Goroka museum on Airport Road with WWII relics, traditional artefacts and 1930s photos of the first Australian patrols into the Highlands. Hours variable per Wikivoyage.

name: Taekanda Cultural Centre
note: Museum: Enga cultural centre near Wabag with wigs, war shields, masks and a sand-painting workshop. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Western Highlands Cultural Centre
note: Museum: cultural centre in Mount Hagen with a reconstructed village hut and artefacts. No Wikipedia article found.

name: Kavieng
note: Town: capital of New Ireland Province at the northern tip of the island, the main air and sea gateway and base for diving, surfing, fishing and island boat trips; WWII bombing and occupation history.

name: Boluminski Highway
note: Road: the main highway down the east coast of New Ireland from Kavieng to Namatanai, a flat cycling route with inland waterholes such as Fissoa along it. A linear route, pinned at its midpoint.

name: Lihir Group
note: Island group: Lihir, Mahur, Masahet and Sanambiet off the New Ireland coast, a gold-mining island group reached by scheduled flights from Namatanai; named as one of the province's islands, with little visitor infrastructure.

name: Lorengau
note: Town: capital of Manus Province on the edge of Seeadler Harbour, with a market, a garamut dance tradition, sago village visits and the Harbourside Hotel tours.
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Lorengau geo tag (town centre; a town, not an attraction)

name: Manus Island
note: Island: the main island of the Admiralty group, where Lorengau, Seeadler Harbour and the WWII sites are; the province is named for it.

name: Buka Island
note: Island: Buka Island, the arrival point for Bougainville by air and the Buka Passage boat trips; the island has the airport, the tourist office and most places to stay.

name: Buka
note: Town: Buka, the most bustling town in Bougainville and the seat of government since the civil war, with the Buka Market, the Buka Passage boats and waterfront restaurants.

name: Sohano Island
note: Island: Sohano, the most visited island in the Buka Passage, with simple eateries and places to stay, a Japanese war memorial and plane wreck on its northern tip and a short K2 boat ride from Buka.
coordinates_source: OSM place=village "Sohano" (photon; the village node on the island)

name: Mount Balbi
note: Mountain: Mount Balbi (2,715 m), an active volcano in the Emperor Range, the highest in the Bougainville chain, reached by a three-day trek from Wakunai.

name: Yamamoto Bomber Wreck
note: WWII site: the Mitsubishi bomber wreck where Admiral Yamamoto was shot down on 18 April 1943, about 3 km off the east coast road south of Arawa, with a signpost; visible in the jungle.

name: Nissan Island
note: Island: Nissan (Green Island), about 100 km north of Buka, with an American WWII airstrip, relics and a guest house with no telephone booking.

name: Samarai
note: Island: former colonial capital and trading port at the entrance to Milne Bay, a 20-minute walk round, with ruins of its boom-town past and a National Historical Heritage Island listing; reached by boat from Alotau.

name: Tawali
note: Dive site: reef and drop-offs at Tawali on the coast near Alotau, named by the PNG tourism authority as a world-renowned Milne Bay dive site; reached by boat, with the Tawali Leisure and Dive Resort on the bluff above.

name: Normanby Island
note: Island: unspoilt D'Entrecasteaux island with trekking trails, rainforest waterfalls and birdwatching (including the Goldie's bird-of-paradise), with very limited accommodation.

name: Gonubalabala
note: Dive site: Gonubalabala Island waters in Milne Bay, named by the PNG tourism authority as a dive site and a known manta ray location.

name: Fergusson Island
note: Island: geothermal volcanic island reached only by boat, with trekking trails and birdwatching for a rare bird-of-paradise and the Curl-crested Manucode; its hot springs at Deidei are listed separately.

name: Trobriand Islands
note: Island group: the Kiriwina Islands, raised coral atolls in the north of Milne Bay known as the Islands of Love, with yam-harvest dancing, village stays, the Kula ring and white beaches; reached by a twice-weekly PNG Air flight from Alotau.

name: Louisiade Archipelago
note: Archipelago: about 100 islands in the far southeast of Milne Bay, a diver's paradise and yachting destination with coral reefs; few visitors and reached mainly by private yacht, so a region rather than a single stop.

name: Misima Island
note: Island: the most populated and most accessible Louisiade island, served by air to Bwagaoia with a guest house; a closed gold mine and island-hopping stop named by the PNG tourism authority.

name: Goodenough Island
note: Island: volcanic island of the D'Entrecasteaux group with rainforest, waterfalls, Mount Vineuo and good birdwatching; named as an unspoilt island to explore and a tour destination from Alotau.

name: Woodlark Island
note: Island group: remote Woodlarks to the north of the province, known for wood carvings and coral reefs, listed as an other destination in Wikivoyage's Milne Bay guide.

name: Coastwatchers Lighthouse
note: Landmark: working lighthouse on Madang harbour, a memorial to the WWII coastwatchers.

name: Madang Central Market
note: Market: busy local market in the centre of Madang, open daily, with produce brought in from the Highlands.

name: Krangket Island
note: Island: five-minute boat trip from Madang; two villages with gardens, a lagoon beach and a basic lodge.

name: USS Boston Wreck
note: Wreck dive: US Navy minesweeper (converted Liberty ship) sunk on a reef drop-off off Madang, about 30 m deep.

name: Balek Wildlife Sanctuary
note: Nature: village wildlife sanctuary about 30 minutes from Madang, where a sulphur creek runs through a limestone cave to a clear stream with turtles and eels; tours via Melanesian Tourist Services.

name: Magic Passage
note: Dive site: narrow drift-dive passage about five minutes by boat from Madang Resort, with coral gardens and garden eels.

name: Karkar Island
note: Island: volcanic island 30 km off Madang with a caldera volcano (last big eruptions 1974-75), a ring road and views back to Madang; known for bilums.

name: Lae
note: Town: PNG's second city and Morobe's capital, at the start of the Highlands Highway; gateway to the Highlands and Huon Gulf.

name: Lae Botanic Gardens
note: Gardens: city gardens in central Lae with PNG plants, birds and an old aeroplane; not always open to the public (Wikipedia).

name: Lae War Cemetery
note: Cemetery: Commonwealth war cemetery with about 2,800 WWII burials, next to the botanic gardens and including the Lae Memorial.

name: Rainforest Habitat
note: Wildlife: 10-hectare animal and bird display at Lae University of Technology, with about 80 birds of paradise in a rainforest enclosure.

name: Black Cat Track
note: Trail: rough 3-4 day overland trek from Salamaua to Wau, a gold-rush and WWII route now used by experienced trekkers.

name: Wau
note: Town: gold-rush town at about 1,100 m, the Black Cat Track's inland end, with the Wau Ecology Institute nearby.

name: Bulolo
note: Town: former gold-dredging town on the Bulolo River, 32 km north-west of Wau, with dredge relics and a golf course.

name: Bulolo Gold Dredges
note: Relic: eight 2,000-tonne gold dredges airlifted into the Bulolo valley; some abandoned in the valley and still visible (Wikivoyage).

name: Tavurvur
note: Volcano: active stratovolcano above Rabaul with a drive-up parking point, hot springs and ash views; Wikivoyage 'See' item 1.

name: Kokopo
note: Town: current provincial capital and airport gateway (Tokua), with markets and the Kokopo war museum; covered in Wikivoyage 'Rabaul'.

name: Rabaul Volcano Observatory
note: Lookout: volcano observatory on Mount Tavanabatir with a view over Rabaul town, bay and volcano; Wikivoyage 'See' item 6 and 'Do' climb.

name: Japanese Barge Tunnel
note: WWII tunnel: Japanese tunnel near Mount Vulcan with barges still inside at Karavia; Wikivoyage 'See' item 3.
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap node (Overpass) tourism=attraction "Japanese WWII Barges Tunnel"

name: New Guinea Club Museum
note: Museum: 1937 New Guinea Club building now a museum of Rabaul's history, with photographs; Wikivoyage 'See' item 5.

name: Bitapaka War Cemetery
note: War cemetery: Australian War Graves Commission cemetery for WWII servicemen of many nations, with a Japanese war memorial; Wikivoyage 'See' item 2.

name: Kokopo War and Cultural Museum
note: Museum: Japanese war relics and photographs in central Kokopo; Wikivoyage 'See' item 7.

name: Duke of York Islands
note: Island group: 45 minutes by boat from Kokopo, for diving, snorkelling and picnics; PNG Tourism 'East New Britain' page.

name: Kimbe
note: Town: capital of West New Britain on Kimbe Bay, main gateway and base for diving; Wikivoyage 'Kimbe'.

name: Kimbe Bay
note: Dive area: bay with 400+ coral and 900+ fish species, WWII wrecks and dolphins; Wikivoyage 'Kimbe' Do (diving).

name: Garbuna Volcano
note: Volcano: still-active volcano near Hoskins with trekking and geothermal features; PNG Tourism West New Britain page.

name: Owers' Corner
note: Trail start/end: the southern trailhead at Owers' Corner (Central Province, 50 km east of Port Moresby) with the monument where the track starts; every guided walk begins or ends here.

name: Isurava
note: Battle site and village: the Isurava war memorial and museum on the track, the site of the 1942 Battle of Isurava; Wikivoyage notes it is hard not to weep at the memorial site.

name: Kokoda
note: Town: station town at the northern end of the Kokoda Track, the only airfield on the track, and the finishing point of most walks.

name: Popondetta
note: Town: the Oro Province capital and gateway, with Girua Airport flights from Port Moresby and the road to Kokoda; the tourism site calls it a base rather than a sight.

name: Tufi
note: Town: fishing and dive town on the Cape Nelson peninsula, base for the Tufi fjords, reef dives and tapa-cloth making; Wikivoyage calls it the Fjordland of Papua New Guinea.

name: Tufi Fjords
note: Scenic feature: drowned river valleys (rias) over 90 m deep with rainforest sides, cruised or kayaked from Tufi; a separate scenic draw from the town itself.

name: Buna
note: Village: coastal village and the Kokoda Track trailhead, with WWII relics and a memorial plaque to the 32nd Division; the tourism site says to visit Buna and Gona.

name: Gona
note: Village: coastal village and WWII battle site where Japanese forces landed in 1942; the tourism site names it with Buna as a place to visit WWII relics.

name: Wewak
note: Town: provincial capital of East Sepik and the gateway for Sepik River trips and the Wewak islands; WWII Japanese airbase and surrender site.

name: Vanimo
note: Town: capital of Sandaun Province on the Indonesian border; base for the surf breaks and the coastal headlands.

name: Maprik
note: Town and district: the Maprik area holds the best-known haus tambaran spirit houses; Wikipedia article is the district.

name: Sepik River
note: River: the Sepik, PNG's longest river, visited by motor-canoe and riverboat trips to river villages; a long linear feature, pin at its main visitor access (Wewak, Angoram, Pagwi). Pinned at Angoram, a river-town access point, not the river centroid.
coordinates_source: osm:node/2643833870 Angoram (river visitor access point, not the river centroid); Wikipedia article Sepik

name: Kairiru Island
note: Island: volcanic island 30 minutes by boat off Wewak with waterfalls, snorkelling and natural hot springs (PTPA); guesthouse per Wikivoyage. Wikipedia title 'Kairiru' is the language.

name: Mushu Island
note: Island: coral atoll with a white-sand beach and reef fish, half an hour off Wewak; basic guesthouse. Named Muschu by PTPA. Wikipedia title is the Disney character.

name: Cape Wom
note: WWII memorial: peace park where General Adachi signed the Japanese surrender in New Guinea in 1945, with open Japanese tunnels; PTPA calls it the Wom Memorial and Japanese Peace Park.
coordinates_source: osm:node/11799415670 monument (Cape Wom Memorial); agrees with Wikipedia within 100 m

name: Vanimo Surf Breaks
note: Surf breaks: consistent reef and point breaks west of Vanimo, up to 3 m, best September to March (Wikivoyage); experienced surfers only.
coordinates_source: osm:node/1250713739 natural=cape Vanimo Point (area point; surf breaks not named in any source)

name: Daru
note: Town: provincial capital of Western Province on Daru Island at the Fly River mouth, and the domestic air gateway to the province. PNG Tourism calls it the 'Wild Wild West' of PNG; Wikivoyage says it has little to interest visitors beyond fishing. Also covers Daru Island (same island, not a separate spot).

name: Kiunga
note: Town: river port on the Fly River and southern end of the Kiunga-Tabubil Highway, known as a base for birdwatching (Wikivoyage) and for nature tours (Kiunga Nature Tours is based here, per PNG Tourism).

name: Lake Murray
note: Natural lake: Papua New Guinea's largest lake (about 647 km2 in the dry season, up to five times that in the wet season), surrounded by wetlands and rainforest. Wikivoyage lists it for birdwatching, fishing and village visits; access is normally by charter aircraft through a lodge.

name: Tonda Wildlife Management Area
note: Protected wetland: PNG's largest protected area, a Ramsar site on the Indonesian border with over 250 waterbird species and savanna wildlife. PNG Tourism lists 'Visit the Tonda Wildlife Management Area'; visits are based at Bensbach Wildlife Lodge.
